skill.name: project-structure
skill.description: Organize project and source folders with safe cleanup rules and common frontend architecture patterns, including Next.js App Router, Bulletproof React, and Feature-Sliced Design.
skill.summary: Plan safe project folder structures for new or messy codebases.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: The static scan reported command, network, filesystem, and sensitive-file patterns, but review found them in Markdown examples, folder diagrams, and reference links. The command guidance uses hardcoded setup or move examples and explicitly forbids deletion in favor of _legacy. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be copied without path review.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit reminder before workflow commands that users must confirm exact source and destination paths.

remediation.issue: Bash is available for a documentation-heavy skill.
remediation.suggestion: Keep deletion commands prohibited and prefer move-only cleanup steps with dated _legacy folders.

content.value_statement: Messy repositories make navigation, ownership, and refactoring harder. This skill provides safe folder layouts and cleanup workflows for JavaScript and frontend projects.
actual_capabilities: Recommends development root folders such as ~/dev, ~/code, ~/workspace, and ~/git.
Provides folder patterns for Next.js App Router, Bulletproof React, Feature-Sliced Design, and hybrid frontend projects.
Lists cleanup commands that inspect folders, create structure, and move old files into _legacy.
Shows naming conventions for folders, React components, hooks, constants, and utility files.
Identifies organization anti-patterns such as desktop folders, language-only grouping, and type-only grouping.
Includes reference links to the underlying architecture documentation.
limitations: It does not analyze runtime code quality or dependency security.
It focuses mainly on JavaScript and TypeScript frontend repositories.
Move commands can change files, so users should approve exact paths first.
External references require network access when opened.

use_cases.title: Set up a new frontend project
use_cases.description: Create a clear starting layout for a React or Next.js application before source files grow.

use_cases.title: Clean a messy repository
use_cases.description: Move outdated folders into _legacy and reshape source files around features or routes.

use_cases.title: Standardize team conventions
use_cases.description: Compare common architecture patterns and document a shared folder strategy for contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-structure skill to propose folders for a new React app. Explain why each top-level folder exists.

prompt_templates.title: Reorganize a messy repository
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup for an existing codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository structure and suggest a safer layout. Move obsolete items to _legacy instead of deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an architecture pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Team decision across frontend structure options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Next.js colocation, Bulletproof React, and Feature-Sliced Design for this product. Recommend one folder strategy with tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a staged migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged migration plan from type-based folders to feature-based folders. Include file move groups, checks, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: I need a folder plan for a new Next.js dashboard.
output: Recommended route groups for public and dashboard pages.
Shared components stay separate from route-specific components.
Global utilities belong in lib, hooks, and types.

output_examples.input: My React project has many components and hooks in top-level folders.
output: Suggested a feature-based layout for auth, users, and dashboard areas.
Moved obsolete folders to a dated _legacy area in the plan.
Highlighted checks to run before applying moves.

output_examples.input: Our team is choosing between Bulletproof React and Feature-Sliced Design.
output: Compared team size, domain complexity, and rule overhead.
Recommended the lighter feature-based pattern for faster adoption.
Listed migration risks and naming standards.

best_practices: Review every move command before running it against a real repository.
Choose one primary grouping rule, such as route, feature, or domain.
Keep removed or uncertain code in dated _legacy folders until reviewed.
anti_patterns: Running deletion commands during structure cleanup.
Mixing work, personal, and study projects in one unlabeled folder.
Putting every component, hook, and utility into global type-based folders.

faq.question: Does this skill delete files?
faq.answer: No. The guidance explicitly forbids deletion and recommends moving old items into _legacy.

faq.question: Which project types fit best?
faq.answer: It fits frontend and full-stack JavaScript projects, especially React and Next.js codebases.

faq.question: Can it organize monorepos?
faq.answer: It can suggest high-level folder boundaries, but it does not provide a full monorepo package strategy.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: It includes command examples for folders and starter files. Users should review paths before execution.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No for local organization. Internet access is only needed to open the listed reference links.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
